newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress party concedes defeat in Punjab.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress party concedes defeat in Punjab.

text.p: India's Congress party conceded on Sunday it had lost a key assembly election in the northern state of Punjab to the region's pro-Sikh Akali Dal party.
"I would like to concede victory to the Akali Dal," Congress general secretary Ghulam Nabi Azad told state-run Doordarshan television. "We may have lost, but the democracy has won."
By 10.30 pm (1700 GMT) the Akali Dal had won 42 seats in the 117-member state assembly, Punjab's chief election official Brajendra Singh told Reuters in the state capital Chandigarh.
The Dal's junior ally in the state, India's main opposition rightwing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) , had won 11 seats from the available results .
Meanwhile the state's ruling Congress party, which won 87 seats in the 1992 state polls, was way behind with six wins.
